svg.text: Amu Darya and Syr Darya · 7,445 level-12 basins · adapted from the Water Flow Diagram method (waterflowdiagram.ch)
This diagram does not close, and is not made to — see the note beneath it.
1 · What arrives, and what is taken from it
22-year mean annual volumes over 965,725 km² (measured) against the 2022 hydrological year of recorded diversion (administered). Colour is how the flow is known. 1 mm of width ≈ 0.33 km³/yr.

path.title: Evapotranspiration — 219 km³/yr (measured) TerraClimate actual evapotranspiration, 22 complete years

Climatic surplus — 93.3 km³/yr (derived) precipitation - evapotranspiration Not a renewable-resource figure: it neither routes water nor accounts for storage, glacier melt or inflow from outside the domain
Amu Darya diverted — 44.3 km³/yr (administered) 44.26 of a 55.23 limit, 80 per cent

Unaccounted difference — 35.2 km³/yr (derived) climatic surplus - recorded diversion A residual, not a resource. The runoff series puts the land-surface flux at 153.7 km3/yr, well above the surplus, which is how visible the model mismatch is at this scale.
Syr Darya diverted — 13.8 km³/yr (administered) 86 per cent of the established limit

rect.title: Amu Darya diversion ICWC/BWO, 2022 hydrological year

Not accounted for The difference between the climatic surplus and recorded diversion. It includes river outflow, wetland and delta losses, aquifer recharge, and the mismatch between two models on different grids. It is not spare water.
Syr Darya diversion ICWC/BWO, 2022 hydrological year

svg.text: 2 · Who takes it, and where the rivers end

ICWC figures for 2022 throughout, so the widths are comparable. Colour is the country. The Syr Darya total is bounded at the Shardara reservoir and therefore excludes Kazakhstan, which lies downstream — its 2022 actual is not published. 1 mm of width ≈ 0.15 km³/yr.

path.title: Turkmenistan — 18.5 km³/yr (administered) Against a limit of 21.83
Uzbekistan — 16.8 km³/yr (administered) Against a limit of 23.57
Withdrawn above Chardara — 13.8 km³/yr (administered) Excludes Kazakhstan, which lies downstream of the reservoir
Tajikistan — 8.99 km³/yr (administered) Against a limit of 9.83
To the delta — 2.06 km³/yr (administered) 2.055 km3 reached the delta in 2022
To the Northern Aral — 0.82 km³/yr (administered) 0.82 km3 in 2022, per Kazakhstan's water authorities
To the Large Aral — 0.503 km³/yr (administered) 0.5035 km3, down from 0.65 in 2021, and sourced entirely from drainage canals rather than river discharge

Kazakhstan, downstream — not quantified (unquantified) The 2022 actual for Kazakhstan below Chardara is not published. Its 2026 limit is 1.369 km3/yr. Drawn as a gap because the diagram cannot honestly give it a width.

rect.title: Amu Darya diversion ICWC/BWO, 2022 hydrological year
Syr Darya diversion ICWC/BWO, 2022 hydrological year

Withdrawn above Chardara Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. The published 2022 total is bounded at the Shardara reservoir and is not split by country; the country figures available are 2026 limits, tabulated separately rather than drawn at a width that would imply they are the same year.
Kazakhstan Downstream of Chardara. Its withdrawal is outside the 13.83 km3 above, and is published as a limit rather than an actual.
Northern Aral Sea Fed by the Syr Darya below Chardara
Large Aral Sea Inflow in 2022 came entirely from drainage canals, not from river discharge

svg.text: 3 · Where Uzbekistan's Amu Darya water goes

Its own scale again: these flows are twenty times smaller than panel 1. Sector shares are national, applied to one basin's diversion — proportions, not basin measurements. 1 mm of width ≈ 0.05 km³/yr.

path.title: Agriculture — 13.3 km³/yr (derived) 14.705 km3 x 90.5% National share of 90.5 per cent applied to what remains of the country's Amu Darya diversion. The share is national; the diversion is one basin. Treat the split as indicative of proportion, not as a basin measurement.
Collector-drainage reuse — 1.6 km³/yr (administered) Reused collector and drainage water, nationally
Returned via drains — 1.6 km³/yr (administered)

Municipal — 0.662 km³/yr (derived) 14.705 km3 x 4.5% National share of 4.5 per cent applied to what remains of the country's Amu Darya diversion. The share is national; the diversion is one basin. Treat the split as indicative of proportion, not as a basin measurement.

Industry — 0.206 km³/yr (derived) 14.705 km3 x 1.4% National share of 1.4 per cent applied to what remains of the country's Amu Darya diversion. The share is national; the diversion is one basin. Treat the split as indicative of proportion, not as a basin measurement.

Fisheries — 0.176 km³/yr (derived) 14.705 km3 x 1.2% National share of 1.2 per cent applied to what remains of the country's Amu Darya diversion. The share is national; the diversion is one basin. Treat the split as indicative of proportion, not as a basin measurement.
Treated wastewater return — 0.156 km³/yr (measured) 428,531 m3/d across 53 plants in 43 basins, 61.7 L/person/day. The one urban flow published in volume here.
Discharged to rivers — 0.156 km³/yr (measured) Outfalls located to level-12 basins

Other — 0.147 km³/yr (derived) 14.705 km3 x 1.0% National share of 1.0 per cent applied to what remains of the country's Amu Darya diversion. The share is national; the diversion is one basin. Treat the split as indicative of proportion, not as a basin measurement.

Thermal Power — 0.074 km³/yr (derived) 14.705 km3 x 0.5% National share of 0.5 per cent applied to what remains of the country's Amu Darya diversion. The share is national; the diversion is one basin. Treat the split as indicative of proportion, not as a basin measurement.

Distribution losses — not quantified (unquantified) Central to the method and often the largest single finding in its published applications. No baseline is published for this region: the 2023 national plan targets a 10 per cent reduction without stating what from.

Groundwater abstraction — not quantified (unquantified) The method separates surface from groundwater sources. National usable groundwater is given as 0.5 km3/yr against an estimated 27.6 km3/yr yield, but abstraction is not published at any scale this diagram can use.

Untreated wastewater — not quantified (unquantified) The inventory carries 53 plants and the volume they treat. What is generated and never reaches a plant is the quantity the method most wants and no source here reports.

rect.title: Uzbekistan sectoral use Sectoral shares are national and are applied here to what remains of the country's Amu Darya diversion after the delta

Distribution losses Central to the method and often the largest single finding in its published applications. No baseline is published for this region: the 2023 national plan targets a 10 per cent reduction without stating what from.

Groundwater abstraction The method separates surface from groundwater sources. National usable groundwater is given as 0.5 km3/yr against an estimated 27.6 km3/yr yield, but abstraction is not published at any scale this diagram can use.
Untreated wastewater The inventory carries 53 plants and the volume they treat. What is generated and never reaches a plant is the quantity the method most wants and no source here reports.
Returned to rivers and the delta

svg.text: Returned to rivers and the delta 1.76
Panels 1 and 3 — how the flow is known
MeasuredThis project's observation record or plant inventory. Reproducible from the published release.
AdministeredPublished by the bodies that allocate the water. What was allocated and diverted, not an independent measurement of what flowed.
DerivedArithmetic on the above, with the operation stated on the flow.
Not quantifiedA flow the method expects and no source here supplies. Drawn as a gap rather than omitted, so its absence is visible.
Dashed hairlines are flows nobody has quantified — drawn at a fixed width so they are never read as small. Each panel is linear within itself; the three scales differ and each is stated.
